Hi Sophie — really appreciate the clear summary. Good to confirm the procurement timeline. A quick recap from our side and concrete next steps: 

Recap: 
- Hosted API: We have hosted clusters in AWS eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) and eu-west-1 (Ireland). Hosted supports EU-region residency for request handling and tokenization, but note: certain managed services (control plane logging, analytics ingestion) are multi-region by default unless explicitly scoped. We can contract to restrict control-plane telemetry to EU only for enterprise customers (legal/contractual addendum).
- Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPU pools provisioned in a customer's chosen cloud region (we can lock to eu-central-1). Provides predictable throughput and can be configured to restrict all data plane traffic to the selected region — useful if you want us to guarantee no cross-region writes.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full private deployment (customer VPC or on-prem appliance) is the standard when in-country data sovereignty + strict network controls are required. This removes any cross-region route risk and gives you control of KMS, audit logs, and network egress rules.

Answers to your questions: 
1) In-country hosting: We currently offer EU-region hosting (Frankfurt and Dublin). For strict in-country (Germany-only) residency, the Private option (VPC or on-prem) is the reliable path. That said, for customers with contractual residency requirements we can negotiate a dedicated eu-central-1-only Hosted plan with contractual controls + audit commitments.

2) Dedicated capacity: We can give a committed GPU pool in eu-central-1 with canary rollouts and fallback routing kept within EU (no cross-region). I'll have Aditya share the typical throughput profiles and pricing bands.

3) Procurement docs: attaching a short EU region matrix and our SOC2 summary. For procurement we typically need: security questionnaire, network requirements, PO + SOW for Dedicated/Private, and a signed addendum for data residency controls.

Next steps: 
- Aditya to share technical routing and network requirements (see attachment network_requirements.xlsx)
- Rishi to coordinate any SOC2 / compliance evidence (SOC2_summary.pdf attached)
- Suggest a procurement + tech follow-up call early next week to lock on Dedicated vs Private and timeline.

If you can confirm the must-have items (in-country requirement vs EU-only acceptable), we can put together 2 options (Dedicated locked to eu-central-1 + Private VPC) with ballpark pricing and timelines.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Sophie — quick technical notes to clarify routing/ops behavior so procurement can assess risk: 

- Hosted routing: By default, Redwood's API gateway routes requests to the nearest healthy serving pool. For EU customers this will normally be eu-central-1 or eu-west-1. However, in extreme failover conditions we support cross-region fallback (e.g., to a different EU zone or, only if explicitly enabled, to other regions). We can disable non-EU fallback entirely for your tenant.
- KV / cache behavior: Prefix caching and KV cache replication are configurable; we can ensure caches are seeded only in EU pools for Dedicated or Hosted scoped plans.
- Control plane telemetry: Can be restricted to EU-only as Marissa mentioned, but requires the residency addendum and changed retention policies for logs/analytics.
- On-prem considerations: If you go Private on-prem, we will provide a hardened runtime image, KMS integration instructions, and an audit log collector config. You'll want to confirm inbound/outbound ports in network_requirements.xlsx (attached).

Ballpark timelines: 
- Hosted: can enable EU-scoped residency within 2-3 weeks with contract addendum.
- Dedicated (reserved pool): provisioning + testing ~ 4-6 weeks depending on GPU availability and SSO/KMS integrations.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 6-10 weeks for delivery and validation depending on on-prem approvals.

I'll drop the network_requirements.xlsx and a short ops checklist to the drive link Marissa shared. Happy to walk your infra team through the ports and KMS flow on the procurement call.

Thanks,
Aditya
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
